name: gap_continuation_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: When a stock gaps up/down on genuine institutional flow (above-average pre-open volume, gap aligned with sector/index direction), the gap often continues for another 0.5-1.0% as momentum traders pile in and VWAP algorithms begin accumulating. This is the 'gap and go' pattern. The key filter is volume: gaps on 2x+ average volume signal real institutional interest, not retail noise. The inefficiency exists because most traders are either fading the gap (contrarian bias) or waiting too long to enter (confirmation bias), allowing early momentum entrants to capture the continuation move before the crowd arrives. Entering within the first 10 minutes with volume confirmation captures this window.
mechanism: Large opening gaps that hold above the prior range indicate a genuine overnight revaluation. Participants who missed the gap chase the move, while short-sellers who are wrong-footed cover into the trend. The resulting buy pressure sustains the gap direction for the first 30-60 minutes until the new equilibrium is established.

indicators.name: rel_strength
indicators.formula: gap_pct - NIFTY_gap_pct  # stock gap relative to index

exit.signal_exit: if EMA_5 crosses EMA_13 against position direction, exit

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX > 13 (need some volatility for continuation); VIX < 25 (not chaotic)

weaknesses: Win rate is below 55% — momentum continuation fails frequently, and the strategy relies on occasional large winners to offset more frequent small losers (emotionally difficult)
The 5-minute opening range breakout gives a delayed entry; by the time the breakout is confirmed, 30-40% of the continuation move may already be done
On days where initial momentum is due to a single large block trade (not genuine flow), the continuation fails and reverses sharply, hitting stops
prior_art: Katz & McCormick (2000) gap and go; Clenow (2014) momentum strategies. Similar to Bulkowski (2005) gap continuation patterns in Technical Analysis.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
